root_cause.text: The PCI endpoint NTB function driver does not check the return value of alloc_workqueue(), so if memory allocation fails, it stores a NULL workqueue pointer that later causes a NULL pointer dereference when queue_work() is called in epf_ntb_epc_init().
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds NULL checks after alloc_workqueue() in both pci-epf-ntb.c and pci-epf-vntb.c, returning -ENOMEM on failure. The CVE description explicitly states that without this check, a NULL workqueue pointer leads to a NULL pointer dereference when queue_work() is called.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
PCI: Add WQ_PERCPU to alloc_workqueue() users

Currently work items enqueued by schedule_delayed_work() use "system_wq"
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 78f5d0d5a23dd81106cbe999d9dcd522964a8f1a
Author: Marco Crivellari <marco.crivellari@suse.com>
Date:   Fri Nov 7 15:25:26 2025 +0100

    PCI: Add WQ_PERCPU to alloc_workqueue() users
    
    Currently work items enqueued by schedule_delayed_work() use "system_wq" (a
    per-CPU wq), while queue_delayed_work() uses WORK_CPU_UNBOUND (used when a
    CPU is not specified). The same applies to schedule_work() that is using
    system_wq and queue_work(), that makes use again of WORK_CPU_UNBO
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit only modifies the alloc_workqueue() flags by adding WQ_PERCPU. It does not add a NULL check on the return value of alloc_workqueue(). The line `kpcintb_workqueue = alloc_workqueue(...)` still stores the result without checking for NULL, leaving the NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in epf_ntb_epc_init() when queue_work() is called. Therefore, the vulnerable construct is present and not fixed.

Later, `queue_work(kpcintb_workqueue, ...)` is called in epf_ntb_epc_init_interface() (line ~1146) and `queue_delayed_work(kpcintb_workqueue, ...)` in epf_ntb_cmd_handler(), both of which will dereference the NULL pointer. No NULL check or error handling is present anywhere in the provided code, so the vulnerable construct is present and unfixed.
